summary: F1 confirmed and fixed: Groovy's map subscript coerces a GString key, so a pins dict built with an interpolated values-file path could be read by no subscript in writeVersionPins — the caller was told 'config/dev/values.yaml names no pins' about a file it had plainly named (F1's symmetric branch) and no pin landed. A new @NonCPS normalizePins() turns the whole structure — file paths, YAML paths and values — into real Strings at the entry, so applyPins needs no defence of its own and two spellings of one file name collide rather than silently dropping a file's pins. Witnessed and verified under a portable JVM plus groovy-all 2.4.21 (the version workflow-cps compiles): the method body against KubeCoderDeploy's real stage files with Jenkins steps stubbed — String-keyed and GString-keyed callers now write identical bytes, exactly the seven lines change per file, all fourteen values round-trip through a YAML parser as strings, a re-run pushes nothing, every guard throws before a write, and all seven vars/*.groovy parse. JenkinsPipelineUtils c5bf246; advisory F2 left standing (already close-out B2); close-out S4 records that a JVM is obtainable here, narrowing G2's premise.
